task.ques: Find the current top 3 super-earth planets and give a brief introduction to them.

claude.final_answer:
FINAL: Proxima Centauri b, GJ 411 b, and GJ 887 b are my top three nearby super-Earth picks, ordered by proximity, with one planet per host system.

Checked 28 October 2026. I use proximity as the meaning of “top”; this is a stated selection criterion, not a ranking of habitability. NASA classifies all three as Super Earth planets.

1. Proxima Centauri b — approximately 4.24 light-years away. This planet orbits an M-type star every 11.2 days. NASA’s current fact panel gives a mass of 1.055 Earth masses and a discovery year of 2016. It is an especially interesting nearby example of a planet only slightly more massive than Earth.
Source: https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanet-catalog/proxima-centauri-b/

2. GJ 411 b — about 8 light-years away, as shown in NASA’s planet viewer. Discovered in 2019 using radial velocity measurements, it has a reported minimum mass of 2.69 Earth masses and circles an M-type star every 12.9 days. NASA estimates its radius at 1.45 times Earth’s; that radius is an estimate, not a measured transit radius.
Source: https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanet-catalog/gj-411-b/

3. GJ 887 b — approximately 10.72 light-years away. Discovered in 2020, this super-Earth orbits an M-type star every 9.3 days. NASA’s current fact panel and archive table give a minimum mass of 3.9 Earth masses. Its short orbit makes it an example of how compact planetary systems around small stars can be.
Source: https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanet-catalog/gj-887-b/

Ranking evidence: NASA’s Planetary Systems Composite Data table was sorted by increasing distance, checking planets with reported masses above Earth’s and below 10 Earth masses. Proxima b is listed at 1.30119 parsecs and GJ 887’s planets at 3.28679 parsecs. Converting with 1 parsec ≈ 3.26156 light-years gives 1.30119 × 3.26156 ≈ 4.24 and 3.28679 × 3.26156 ≈ 10.72 light-years. GJ 411 b’s distance was checked against NASA’s planet viewer. GJ 887 c, d, and e share b’s host-system distance; b is the representative selected here.
Catalog: https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/cgi-bin/TblView/nph-tblView?app=ExoTbls&config=PSCompPars

Evidence image: final.png is a genuine NASA GJ 411 b viewport showing its name, Super Earth classification, mass, orbital period, discovery method, and discovery date. It was reduced to 1280 pixels on its long side.
